purpose: Freeze a finite seven-route prevalue review of issuer-as-utility-provider customer connection, meter, delivery, billing, arrears, interruption and restoration states without reading research values or manufacturing a factor from adjacent terminal domains.

repository_evidence.bounded_search_scope: Campaign160 inventory and Campaign163-203 source-frontier metadata only
repository_evidence.environment_asset_license_and_incident_b: Campaign165, Campaign166, Campaign178 and Campaign179 freeze environmental outputs, discrete operational incidents, productive assets and licenses or concessions. Generation, network capacity, an asset, a concession or a reported outage does not preserve service-point application, connection, meter, delivery, interruption, bill, arrears, disconnection, reconnection and restoration identities across the complete applicable customer population.
repository_evidence.operating_kpi_boundary: Campaign168 freezes recurring volume, utilization and adoption KPIs. Aggregate customers, connections, meters, electricity or gas sold, water supplied, line loss, outage duration or collection rates do not preserve opening stocks and all customer, service-point, meter, read, bill, delinquency, interruption and closure transitions.
repository_evidence.pricing_customer_quality_and_support_bou: Campaign169 freezes tariffs and selling terms, Campaign170 freezes customer experience outcomes, and Campaign199 freezes service-ticket stock flow and SLA clocks. A tariff, satisfaction score, complaint or support ticket cannot substitute for the utility provider's underlying connection, meter, service-delivery, outage, billing and collection lifecycle.
repository_evidence.payment_and_accounting_boundary: Campaign195 freezes authorization, clearing, refund and settlement rails. Cash receipts, receivables, contract assets or liabilities, bad debt, provisions and revenue do not establish a complete customer-premise, service-point, meter-reading, bill, arrears, disconnection and reconnection history.
repository_evidence.generic_service_lifecycle_boundary: Campaign203 demonstrates that superficially similar booking, service, interruption, refund and compensation operators do not create a cross-sector factor. Utility service has distinct premises, connection points, meters, reads, regulated obligations, network topology, outage membership, billing cycles and protected-customer rules and requires its own complete source contract.
repository_evidence.privacy_and_critical_infrastructure_boun: No directly identifiable customer, address, account, payment credential, household occupancy, precise consumption trace, vulnerable-customer record, critical-infrastructure topology, security credential or operational control data may be acquired or used. Any admitted source must be lawful, licensed or public, deidentified and aggregated enough to prevent re-identification and infrastructure-security harm while preserving the frozen point-in-time issuer-state contract.
repository_evidence.sector_scope_boundary: Applicable listed electricity, gas, water, district energy and other regulated network or retail utility providers, listed parents and material operating subsidiaries must be frozen point in time. Generators without retail or network customers, equipment manufacturers, fuel suppliers, construction contractors and structurally inapplicable issuers may not be filled with zero or cross-sector ranked.
repository_evidence.point_in_time_boundary: A current customer count, network map, meter estate, tariff book, outage dashboard, arrears balance or service status cannot be projected backward without application, connection, meter, read, estimate, correction, delivery, interruption, restoration, bill, dispute, payment, arrears, disconnection, reconnection, closure and first-public or first-licensed-availability histories.
